faqs.question: What is the scariest movie on this Halloween list?
faqs.answer: Three films score 5/5: The Exorcist (1973, R/18, 121 minutes), Hereditary (2018, R/15, 127 minutes) and the Spanish found-footage film [REC] (2007, R/18, 78 minutes). Save them for the last weekend of October, after you have worked up the ladder.

faqs.question: Which Halloween movie works for someone who hates horror?
faqs.answer: Pick a 1/5: Practical Magic (1998, PG-13), Young Frankenstein (1974, PG), Edward Scissorhands (1990, PG-13) or What We Do in the Shadows (2014). The last is rated R for bloody violent content, but it plays as comedy rather than fear.

faqs.question: Are there good Indian horror films for Halloween?
faqs.answer: Yes, two from 2018. Tumbbad is a slow, folk-myth horror rated 15 by the BBFC, and Stree is a horror-comedy, also BBFC 15 and 127 minutes, that scores only 2/5 on fear.

faqs.question: Which Halloween movie is actually set on Halloween night?
faqs.answer: Trick 'r Treat (2007) is built around Halloween night, which is why it closes the five-weekend plan on 31 October. It is rated R in the US and 15 by the BBFC, and runs 82 minutes.

faqs.question: Is it legal to watch Nosferatu online?
faqs.answer: In the US, yes: the Copyright Office says all works published in the United States before 1 January 1931 are in the public domain, and Nosferatu dates from 1922. Copyright rules differ by country, and a new restoration or score can carry its own copyright, so check the version you pick.

faqs.question: When do the 1931 Dracula and Frankenstein films enter the public domain?
faqs.answer: In the US, on 1 January 2027, under the same 95-year rule that already covers works published before 1931. Until then, treat them as protected.

faqs.question: Why does a film have a different rating in the US and the UK?
faqs.answer: The MPA and the BBFC are separate bodies with their own standards. Happy Death Day (2017) is PG-13 in the US but 15 in the UK, while A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984) is R in the US and 15 in the UK.

faqs.question: Is it OK to watch horror movies if I get anxious?
faqs.answer: Probably, on current evidence: a 2026 BMC Psychology diary study of 199 adults found no sign that frightening true-crime viewing raised anxiety, though all its effects were small. Start at a low scare level, end each night on the lighter film, and stop if it stops being fun.

faqs.question: Do horror fans have a particular personality?
faqs.answer: One 2025 Cureus study of 300 students in Bengaluru found that preferring horror correlated with extraversion (0.55) and agreeableness (0.71). It is a single small sample, so treat it as a hint rather than a rule.

faqs.question: Which Korean horror movie should I start with?
faqs.answer: Start with Train to Busan (2016, BBFC 15, 118 minutes), a zombie thriller that scores 3/5. Move to A Tale of Two Sisters (2003, R/15, 114 minutes) once you want a slower, scarier 4/5.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Movies to Watch in October, Sorted by Mood and Scare

The best Halloween movies to watch are matched to your nerve: start October on a cosy 1/5 like *Practical Magic* (1998, PG-13) and finish on a 5/5 like *The Exorcist* (1973, R). Below are 27 films in seven moods with year, runtime, MPA and BBFC rating, scare score and a "watch if you liked" pointer, then a five-weekend schedule and three public-domain classics you can watch legally. If you invite someone, expect the link to be opened on a phone: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are, and each is viewed 11.1 times on average (platform-wide, not Halloween data).

## How do you pick a Halloween movie by scare level?

A scare level is a 1–5 score for how hard a film frightens a general adult audience: 1 means no real fear, 5 means sustained dread or graphic horror. It is our editorial judgment, so read it next to the official rating, which describes content rather than fear.

Official ratings carry the detail. The MPA says [rating descriptors have been part of every PG, PG-13, R and NC-17 rating since 1990](https://www.filmratings.com/ratings-guide/), and the BBFC writes a line of content advice for each release. A 2022 PLOS ONE systematic review notes that [the UK has classified films since 1912](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC9067675) and sorts content warnings into 14 domains.

Taste matters too. In a 2025 Cureus study of 300 Bengaluru students aged 20 to 23, [a preference for horror correlated with extraversion (0.55) and agreeableness (0.71)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12182957); the authors suggest horror's shared, group viewing as one reason. It is a small correlational sample, but it backs a plan built around company.

## 27 Halloween movies to watch, grouped by mood

Each entry gives year, runtime, US MPA/UK BBFC rating, scare score and a film you may know. Runtimes come from BBFC classifications, and "NR" means that body's search returned no record.

### 1. Cosy and not scary

These suit the first weekend or a friend who hates jump scares. None goes above 1/5.

- **Practical Magic** (1998), 104 min, PG-13/12A, scare 1/5; if you liked *Hocus Pocus*
- **Young Frankenstein** (1974), 105 min, PG/12A, scare 1/5; if you liked *Airplane!*
- **Edward Scissorhands** (1990), 104 min, PG-13/12, scare 1/5; if you liked *The Nightmare Before Christmas*

### 2. Gothic classics

Gothic horror means old houses and secrets, not chases. Atmosphere comes first.

- **The Innocents** (1961), 100 min, NR/12A, scare 3/5; if you liked *The Others*
- **Crimson Peak** (2015), 118 min, R/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *Rebecca*
- **Sleepy Hollow** (1999), 105 min, R/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *Beetlejuice*

### 3. Folk horror

Folk horror puts the threat in a village ritual, often in daylight. It unsettles more than it startles.

- **The Wicker Man** (1973), 84 min, NR/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *Hot Fuzz*
- **The Witch** (2015), 93 min, R/NR, scare 4/5; if you liked *The Crucible*
- **Midsommar** (2019), 146 min, R/18, scare 4/5; if you liked *Get Out*

### 4. Slashers

Slashers are the most predictable genre here, which is the fun. Their ratings run high for violence, not dread.

- **Black Christmas** (1974), 98 min, R/18, scare 4/5; if you liked *When a Stranger Calls*
- **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (1984), 91 min, R/15, scare 4/5; if you liked *Stranger Things*
- **Trick 'r Treat** (2007), 82 min, R/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *Creepshow*
- **Happy Death Day** (2017), 96 min, PG-13/15, scare 2/5; if you liked *Groundhog Day*

### 5. Supernatural

This is the top of the ladder. Two of the four score 5/5, so save them for the last weekend.

- **The Exorcist** (1973), 121 min, R/18, scare 5/5; if you liked *Rosemary's Baby*
- **The Conjuring** (2013), 111 min, R/15, scare 4/5; if you liked *Insidious*
- **The Babadook** (2014), 93 min, NR/15, scare 4/5; if you liked *The Sixth Sense*
- **Hereditary** (2018), 127 min, R/15, scare 5/5; if you liked *Midsommar*

### 6. Horror-comedy

Horror-comedy is the safest pick for a mixed group. The laughs land first.

- **Shaun of the Dead** (2004), 99 min, R/15, scare 2/5; if you liked *Zombieland*
- **What We Do in the Shadows** (2014), 85 min, R/15, scare 1/5; if you liked *The Office*
- **Tucker & Dale vs. Evil** (2010), 88 min, R/15, scare 2/5; if you liked *The Cabin in the Woods*

### 7. International horror: Japan, Korea, Spain and India

Subtitles keep phones down, so these work well for groups. Years are production years as the BBFC records them.

- **Kwaidan** (Japan, 1964), 183 min extended cut, NR/PG, scare 2/5; if you liked *Spirited Away*
- **A Tale of Two Sisters** (South Korea, 2003), 114 min, R/15, scare 4/5; if you liked *The Sixth Sense*
- **Train to Busan** (South Korea, 2016), 118 min, NR/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *World War Z*
- **The Orphanage** (Spain, 2007), 105 min, R/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *The Devil's Backbone*
- **[REC]** (Spain, 2007), 78 min, R/18, scare 5/5; if you liked *The Blair Witch Project*
- **Tumbbad** (India, 2018), 107 min, NR/15, scare 3/5; if you liked *Pan's Labyrinth*
- **Stree** (India, 2018), 127 min, NR/15, scare 2/5; if you liked *Bhool Bhulaiyaa*

## Where to start: one film per scare level

One night only? Pick a row by how much fear you want. Each row is a strong pick under 100 minutes.

| Mood | Film | Year | MPA/BBFC | Scare |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Horror-comedy | What We Do in the Shadows | 2014 | R/15 | 1/5 |
| Slasher | Happy Death Day | 2017 | PG-13/15 | 2/5 |
| Folk horror | The Wicker Man | 1973 | NR/15 | 3/5 |
| Supernatural | The Babadook | 2014 | NR/15 | 4/5 |
| International | [REC] | 2007 | R/18 | 5/5 |

Notice that the rating does not track the scare. *What We Do in the Shadows* is rated R for bloody violent content yet scores 1/5, while *The Babadook* has no MPA rating at all and scores 4/5.

## How to build an October watch schedule, weekend by weekend

October 2027 starts on a Friday, which gives five full weekends ending on Sunday 31 October, Halloween itself (in 2026, Halloween falls on a Saturday). Climb one step per weekend so nobody is thrown in at 5/5.

- **Weekend 1, 2–3 Oct:** cosy plus gothic, such as *Practical Magic* then *The Innocents* (204 minutes)
- **Weekend 2, 9–10 Oct:** horror-comedy plus folk horror, such as *Shaun of the Dead* then *The Wicker Man* (183 minutes)
- **Weekend 3, 16–17 Oct:** international night, either *Kwaidan* alone (183 minutes) or *The Orphanage* then *[REC]* (183 minutes)
- **Weekend 4, 23–24 Oct:** slashers, such as *Black Christmas* then *A Nightmare on Elm Street* (189 minutes)
- **Weekend 5, 30–31 Oct:** *Hereditary* or *The Exorcist* on Saturday, then *Trick 'r Treat* on Halloween night, since it is set on 31 October

End each night on the lighter film if anyone scares easily. Keep runtimes under about 3.5 hours a night, or the second film gets watched half-asleep.

A month of horror is unlikely to wreck anyone's nerves on current evidence. A 2026 BMC Psychology diary study of 199 adults found that [anxiety one day predicted more violent true-crime viewing the next](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13501714), and no evidence that this frightening media raised anxiety, though every effect fell below the authors' threshold for a meaningful size.

## Public-domain Halloween classics you can watch legally

The US Copyright Office's duration circular states that [all works published in the United States before 1 January 1931 are in the public domain](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ15a.pdf). That covers the silent classics below, which the BBFC rates as low as U.

- **Nosferatu** (1922), about 91 min on video, BBFC PG, scare 2/5, the original vampire film
- **The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari** (1920; the BBFC lists it as 1919), about 66 min, BBFC U, scare 2/5, painted, tilted sets that still look strange
- **Night of the Living Dead** (1968), 95 min on DVD, BBFC 15, scare 4/5, the film that set the modern zombie rules

*Night of the Living Dead* is the exception to the 1931 cut-off. It is widely treated as public domain in the US because its 1968 release prints lacked a copyright notice, and the Internet Archive hosts a [copy marked public domain](https://archive.org/details/night_of_the_living_dead_dvd). Two cautions: public-domain status is a US rule and differs by country, and restorations or newly composed scores may be separately copyrighted.

## Why this list names no streaming services

Streaming catalogues change monthly and differ by country, so a "where to watch" line printed for the US is wrong in India or the UK within weeks. A film's year, runtime and rating, by contrast, do not change.

So none of the 30 titles here carries a platform. Search each one in your own apps for your region on the day you watch; only the three public-domain films are near-certain to be findable, because anyone may host them.

## Sending a watch-together invite, and when not to

For one person, the [Halloween card on /happy-halloween](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) works as the invite. After three knocks they carve a pumpkin until your chosen word lights up, find your letter by flashlight in a dark attic, then face the closing question, editable up to 60 characters, so it can name the film; an email reaches you on their first answer.

It has partner, bestie, family and kids modes, holds up to six photos, and ends in a 1080×1920 Boo License. If you want the invite to stay sealed until film night, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds an optional unlock time, a voice note of up to 60 seconds and a 280-character reply box. 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators password-protect their page before sharing, so private invites are normal here.

It is the wrong tool for a group. Both pages are one-person greeting pages in English, not party invitations, so for six friends a group chat with the five-weekend list above does the job better. And if the person is already on your sofa, skip the link and press play.

## Sources

- Menon AS et al. "Association Between One's Preferred Film Genres and Personality Traits." Cureus, 23 May 2025. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12182957)
- Perchtold-Stefan CM et al. "Does true crime increase negative affect, or negative affect lead to true crime?" BMC Psychology, 16 June 2026. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13501714)
- Charles A et al. "Typology of content warnings and trigger warnings: Systematic review." PLOS ONE, 4 May 2022. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC9067675)
- Motion Picture Association. "Ratings Guide." [filmratings.com](https://www.filmratings.com/ratings-guide/)
- US Copyright Office. "Circular 15A: Duration of Copyright." [copyright.gov](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ15a.pdf)
- Internet Archive. "Night of the Living Dead" (1968). [archive.org](https://archive.org/details/night_of_the_living_dead_dvd)

structuralLimitations: SERP: Firecrawl disconnected; 2 WebSearch calls (US-served index, not Google ranking). Query 1 top 10: tvguide.com (2026, 32 films, streaming links, no ratings/runtimes), mentalfloss.com (20 films, no ratings), theforestscout.com (2019 student paper), hcdevilsadvocate.com (2020 student paper, 403 to script fetch, indexed via ctx_fetch_and_index) and 5 hijacked-subdomain spam pages. Fifth page analysed from query 2: filmdaze.net (31 titles, no ratings). Weak in top 10: 7 by the WebSearch index; serps.md measured 3 on Google with imdb/variety/THR/netflix/rottentomatoes, so the real SERP is harder than this index suggests. None of the five gives ratings, runtimes, a scare score, international picks by country or public-domain status.

Ratings: MPA verified per film via filmratings.com search; BBFC rating and runtime via bbfc.co.uk release pages. 'NR' marks no record found: The Innocents, The Wicker Man (1973), The Babadook, Kwaidan, Train to Busan, Tumbbad and Stree have no MPA hit; The Witch has no BBFC hit. Black Christmas's MPA R is filed under its 1975 alternate title Stranger in the House. The Witch runtime (93 min) is from Wikidata, not BBFC. Practical Magic's BBFC 12A and 104 min are from its 2026 cinema re-release record; Tumbbad's BBFC 15 / 107 min record carries production year 2024 (its re-release), not 2018. Runtimes vary by cut (The Wicker Man 84 min is the 2007 cinema version; Kwaidan 183 min is the extended version).

Night of the Living Dead: the reason it is public domain (1968 prints without a copyright notice) could not be fetched from a primary source today: loc.gov returned 503 (Columbus Day outage), smithsonianmag and pghcitypaper 403, Google Books quota exhausted. The post therefore says it is 'widely treated as' public domain and links the Internet Archive copy carrying a public-domain mark; archive.org is a cap-exempt reference host, and the mark is uploader-applied. Re-check against the Library of Congress National Film Registry essay when loc.gov is up.

Coordinator note applied: halloween-movie-quotes already cites Scrivner 2020 (PMC7492010), Duke Public Domain Day and copyright.gov Circular 33, so this post drops Scrivner and Duke and uses Circular 15A (a different copyright.gov URL; copyright.gov now in 2 posts). The 1931 Dracula/Frankenstein 2027 date appears only as one FAQ line. Main list avoids the quotes post's films (Halloween 1978, The Shining, Scream, Nosferatu, NOTLD as main entries) and Batch 1's halloween-movies-for-kids 23 films; NOTLD and Nosferatu appear only in the public-domain section the prompt requires.

Research: the 'why people watch horror' slot is weaker than the spent papers. Cureus (Menon 2025) is correlational, n=300, one city; BMC Psychology (Perchtold-Stefan 2026) studies true crime, framed in the paper as frightening media, not horror films. Frontiers (PMC11185070, PMC6582762) and SAGE Evolutionary Psychology (PMC11155347) candidates were rejected per BRIEF §9.

Scare scores (1–5) and 'watch if you liked' pairings are editorial judgment, stated as such in the body. Calendar: 1 October 2027 is a Friday and 31 October 2027 a Sunday (computed); 31 October 2026 is a Saturday.
